answer: Fork-Mirror Registration. Each new agent identity must submit a small task trace that is replayed against the existing population; if the trace lands on an occupied behavioural terrace, registration stalls until the overlap is explained. Duplicates become visible as a mirror of a prior trace, and a flagged cluster starts a reputation cost spiral where every linked identity loses standing. An attacker must then generate genuinely distinct task traces per identity, paying the full generation cost each time instead of copying one.
